reading.title: The Four-Day Week
reading.text:
Several companies around the world have experimented with a four-day working week, in which employees work fewer hours for the same salary. In one large trial involving more than sixty organisations, most participating companies reported that productivity stayed the same or improved. Employees said they felt less stressed and had more time for family and exercise.

However, the model does not suit every type of business. Hospitals, shops and other services that must be available every day found it harder to organise shifts. Some managers also worried that customers would be unhappy if staff were less available. Supporters argue that careful planning can solve most of these problems, and many companies in the trial decided to continue with the shorter week after it ended.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Good afternoon, City Tourist Office. How can I help?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Hi, I'd like to book the boat tour for tomorrow, please. For two adults.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Certainly. There are tours at ten o'clock and at two o'clock. The morning tour is fully booked, I'm afraid.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Then the afternoon one is fine. How much does it cost?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: It's eighteen pounds per person. The tour lasts about ninety minutes and leaves from Pier Four, next to the old lighthouse.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: A warm jacket is a good idea. It can be windy on the water, even in summer.
